text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called a "silent killer" because most people do not have any symptoms. You can live with high blood pressure for years without feeling sick or noticing anything is wrong.
snippet_highlighted_words: most people do not have any symptoms

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms During Dangerously High Blood Pressure (Hypertensive Crisis)
Symptoms usually only appear if your blood pressure rises to extreme levels (typically above 180/120 mm Hg). These signs may include:

list.snippet: Vision changes (such as blurred or double vision)
Sudden confusion, numbness, or weakness (which can signal a stroke)

text_blocks.snippet: Some people with chronically high blood pressure may experience subtle or easy-to-dismiss signs, such as:

list.snippet: Pounding sensations in the chest, neck, or ears

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do in an Emergency
According to the American Heart Association:

list.snippet: If your blood pressure reading is above 180/120 mm Hg, wait one minute and recheck it.
If it remains that high and you have emergency symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, vision changes, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking, call 911 immediately.
If your reading is above 180/120 mm Hg but you feel fine, contact your healthcare provider right away.

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms are rare, the only reliable way to check for high blood pressure is through regular readings at a doctor's office or with an approved home monitor, as outlined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
